newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China to announce Taiwan shippers list - paper.
newsitem.headline: China to announce Taiwan shippers list - paper.

text.p: China will announce on April 17 a list of 11 Taiwan and mainland shippers allowed to sail directly across the Taiwan Strait, Taiwan's China Times reported on Friday.
The paper quoted unidentified sources as saying China will issue permits to seven Taiwan and four China shipping companies to operate direct shipping business across the strait.
Taiwan has banned such links since 1949, when the Nationalists were defeated by the Chinese communists in a civil war and driven off the mainland.
Despite the ban, indirect cross-strait trade and investment ties have flourished since a political thaw began in the late 1980s.

Yang Ming Marine, Uniglory Marine, Wan Hai Lines and Chinese Maritime Transport Ltd and three other Taiwan firms were listed by the newspaper that would be given the permission by China for direct shipping.
China Ocean Shipping Co, China National Foreign Trade Transportation Corp and two other mainland based shippers were also named by the newspaper to be included in China's list.
Taiwan's Transport Minister Tsai Chao-yang was not immediately available for comment.
Taiwan has approved applications by about a dozen Taiwan shippers for direct shipping with China, and these companies are now seeking Beijing's blessing for the links.
Taiwan media said on Thursday Taiwan shipping leaders had begun receiving invitations for an April 8 ceremony in the southern Chinese port city of Xiamen to mark the first direct sailing.
But state radio quoted a senior Chinese Ministry of Communications official as denying a ceremony would be held.
Of the several Taiwan shippers contacted on Thursday by Reuters, none would confirm or deny the report.
The radio said Chinese authorities were still reviewing the Taiwan shippers' applications, but they expected the review would be completed by the end of March.
Under the Taiwan government's plan, direct shipping would involve its southern port of Kaohsiung, and could eventually extend to Taichung port in central Taiwan.
China has agreed to open its ports in the southern coastal cities of Xiamen and Fuzhou for such links.
Xiamen is a flourishing trade gateway and special economic zone in China's Fujian province, which hosts billions of dollars in Taiwan investment.
